messages:
Maya (support): Hi team — customer Jane reports streaming tool-call failures where the JSON args get cut off mid-stream after an auth retry. She sees schema validation errors on our side.
Jane (customer): When I call /v1/streams with function calls enabled, the last chunk sometimes ends in '...\"args\": {\"query\": \"foo' and never closes. Happens on retry after 401 refresh.
Jane (customer): Repro steps: 1) open SSE POST to /v1/streams 2) send messages with tool call 3) force token expiry, client refreshes token and resumes 4) we get schema error.
Maya (support): Thanks. Can you paste the server log lines (request ids) and whether you're going through a proxy?
Jane (customer): Using nginx reverse proxy + our app. Logged request id: req-8f9a1. Proxy config is fairly standard, proxy_buffering on.
Eli (sre): @Maya can you capture the exact error? Is it a parser exception from the runtime or our request runtime rejecting it?
Toolbot: ERROR (runtime): toolcall args JSON parsing failed: unexpected end of input at position 421 -- request_id=req-8f9a1
Noah (infra): Hypothesis: connection resume after token refresh causes the client to re-open the SSE stream but nginx reuses an upstream keepalive socket that partially drained previous chunk causing mid-chunk truncation.
Eli (sre): That matches. We saw similar once when proxy_timeouts + proxy_buffering interacted with chunked SSE. Can you share a minimal curl repro?
Jane (customer): I tried this curl: 
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.example.com/v1/streams -d @payload.json
```
payload.json contains the streaming preface and then an interleaved toolcall json block.
Maya (support): Can you paste the exact partial payload we received (logged) around the time of req-8f9a1?
Jane (customer): Here's truncated payload we logged on our side (redacted):
```
event: response
data: {"id":"c1","type":"tool","name":"search","args":{"query":"how to deploy redwood"
```
...and then connection closed.
Eli (sre): Ok. Two likely vectors: 1) upstream (our runtime) truncated because it detected a connection reset from nginx; 2) nginx buffered and then closed prematurely on backend retry. We need tcp-level capture.
Noah (infra): Quick triage steps we recommend to customer:
- toggle `proxy_buffering off;` for the SSE location
- ensure `proxy_read_timeout` is longer than client token refresh window
- try `proxy_request_buffering off;` if body is streaming
- or route client directly to backend for a test (bypass nginx) to confirm.
Jane (customer): I turned off proxy_buffering and reproduced. Still seeing occasional truncation but less often. Direct-to-backend test looks clean.
Eli (sre): That strongly implicates nginx buffering + keepalive reuse. Another check: are you using HTTP/2 between client and nginx? h2 can multiplex streams and some intermediaries behave oddly with chunked SSE.
Jane (customer): Client->nginx is HTTP/2, nginx->backend is HTTP/1.1 keepalive.
Maya (support): Can you capture the request/response ids from both nginx access logs and our logs at the same times so we can correlate? Also include client-side token refresh timing.
Jane (customer): I exported nginx access logs for the window: lines attached (not in thread). Correlation id mapping: local_xid=abc123 -> our req-8f9a1.
Noah (infra): We'll also check our ingress for any 502/504 or upstream resets around that id. Could be our upstream closed socket during token handshake.
Eli (sre): Temporary mitigation we can suggest: if tool args are critical, use a non-streamed POST RPC (non-SSE) for those calls until we finish. Also we can add server-side stronger validation that attempts to reassemble fragments when resumptions happen, but that's risky.
Maya (support): For a concrete next step, we need: 1) packet capture (tcpdump) from nginx to backend during a failing repro, 2) our runtime logs for req-8f9a1 (we fetched some already), 3) client token refresh timing and method.
Jane (customer): I can run tcpdump and reproduce in a staging env. ETA 4 hours.
Eli (sre): Thanks. Also, send us the exact client library and version. If you're using a generic SSE client that re-opens streams without finishing previous chunk, that could be the culprit.
Jane (customer): Using node-eventsource v2.2.0 and a small custom wrapper. I'll try updating.
Noah (infra): Field note: If nginx reuses a kept-alive upstream connection and the backend closes mid-chunk, nginx might forward the partial chunk to client then tear down. If client then reconnects and resumes sending, the backend could see concatenated fragments leading to invalid JSON at schema level.
Maya (support): We'll mark this as high priority. Eli/Noah — can we instrument the runtime to include a short SHA suffix of the final chunk per request so we can detect mid-chunk truncation vs well-formed closure? Might help triage without packet captures.
Eli (sre): Good idea. I can add a debug flag that logs chunk checksums for streaming sessions. Push a quick patch to staging and we can ask customer to hit staging.
Toolbot: ACTIONS: capture tcpdump, correlate logs, try proxy_buffering off, try direct backend.
Jane (customer): Thanks everyone — I'll run the captures and try direct backend. Will report back with pcap + logs. :thumbsup:
Maya (support): Appreciate it — tagging @eng-runtime if we need deeper runtime changes after the captures. :eyes:
